name: G'MIC
role: CLI filter language with ~1000 procedural filters; stylised and generative looks
summary: Image-processing framework driven by the gmic command line and its own scripting language. Ships roughly a thousand filters (denoise, stylise, tone-map, procedural noise, patterns) and runs them over stills or image sequences, writing standard raster formats. Its strength is filters and generative looks that ImageMagick has no equivalent for; it is not a compositor or a colour-managed pipeline tool.
use_when: Painterly, stylised or procedural filter looks that ImageMagick lacks
Heavy denoise, inpainting or detail-preserving tone mapping on frames
Generating procedural textures or noise fields from the CLI
Applying one filter chain across a numbered frame sequence
avoid_when: Plain resize, crop, convert, montage: ImageMagick is the validated CLI baseline
Colour-managed conversion between spaces: OpenColorIO or oiiotool
Node pipelines needing fast resize and encode: Sharp
Anything needing predictable output across versions: pin the gmic build
license: CeCILL (LGPL-like and GPL-compatible; recheck per component)
notes: 2026-10-26: Homebrew formula gmic exists at 4.0.6, matching the upstream release; macOS build capabilities (OpenMP, optional libs) not verified. gmic.eu page gave no command syntax; learn from the gmic reference.

assessment.rationale: Version 4.0.6 listed on gmic.eu dated 2026-10-14; repository pushed 2026-10-26. Unique filter library not matched by ImageMagick; niche but real for effects.
